AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first proof precedes implementation, in two recorded steps. Step 1: tests/renderer-free backend-only — m017_recent.rs gains the #[cfg(test)] gap-seam hook fn recent_test_gap_park plus its SINGLE call site between the loaded read and the persist inside recent_add_inner (compiling away outside test builds — cfg(test) only, zero production behavior change), armed exclusively by the new pin through a tests-module static channel pair; the pin recent_concurrent_adds_from_two_threads_both_persist is then shown RED on the baseline with cargo test --locked --offline --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --bin mark recent: the parked interleaving deterministically loses one insert. Step 2: the three rename-seam pins are authored against the planned T-002 surface (#[cfg(test)] fn recent_add_inner_with_rename(prefs: &PrefsState, path: &str, rename: &dyn Fn(&Path, &Path) -> std::io::Result<()>) -> Result<(), String> and PrefsState::update_with_rename) and the compile failure is recorded as their red-by-absence evidence (the C-SESSION-DURABILITY get_many precedent). Both red records exist before T-002 lands any implementation.

recent_concurrent_adds_from_two_threads_both_persist is deterministic with NO sleeps, NO busy-waits and NO timing: the pin arms the seam, spawns thread A running the add under test, and dispatches on the FIRST message of one mpsc channel — Ready (sent by the seam hook when A is parked between its read and its persist; the pre-fix shape) → the pin then spawns thread B running a full add, waits for B's completion, sends the seam release and joins both; Done (sent by A's wrapper at completion; the post-fix shape once the seam call site is retired) → the pin spawns B and joins. After join the pin reloads through a fresh PrefsState::from_path over the same tempfile preferences.json and asserts BOTH paths present; survivor order is deliberately not asserted. On the pre-change tree the parked interleaving loses B's insert (A's stale-list store erases it) — red; after the encompassing fix the SAME test body is green by mutex serialization alone — recorded honestly, and the pin never blocks on Ready when the seam is unreachable (a post-fix hang is a design violation, not a pass).

The three rename-seam pins, all carrying the recent_ prefix (review minor 4): recent_unchanged_head_add_skips_the_persist seeds a list with P at head through the fresh_prefs canon, adds P via recent_add_inner_with_rename with a rename closure injected to FAIL, and asserts the call resolves Ok with the reloaded list unchanged in content and order — proof the persist provably never ran, since any rewrite would surface the injected failure; recent_changed_add_still_persists_through_the_seam proves the same failing seam fires exactly when the list changes — a genuinely new path returns Err and an add that only REORDERS (existing path, not at head) also returns Err with the reloaded list showing the new order (recorded honestly as the negative control of the skip pin: against the always-persist pre-fix behavior it is green the moment it compiles); recent_add_performs_at_most_one_save_through_the_seam drives one changed add and one unchanged add through a COUNTING (non-failing) rename closure and asserts at most one rename for the changed add and zero for the unchanged add — a discipline pin, recorded honestly as green both sides once it compiles.

No production behavior change in this task beyond the cfg(test) hook call site; the 18 existing m017 pins stay green throughout step 1 (the hook is inert while disarmed); m005_prefs.rs, recent.ts, project.js and editor.js are untouched in this task; no locale file is touched.
